plan_scope: v2.0.0-rc.3 — guided conversational Harness construction as ONE closed loop: frozen onboarding executor spec (2026-08-04-harness-init-guided-onboarding.md) + rc.3 conversational layer addendum (2026-08-05-rc3-conversational-layer-addendum.md) jointly constitute rc.3's complete product contract. Executor, dialog layer, shell tests, forward eval, and acceptance (F-CONV-01..09) are delivered together. v2.1+ is deferred until v2.0.0 is stable and is NOT pre-seeded here.
fail_closed_start_conditions: master clean (git checkout master && git pull, no local divergences)
target branch 'rc3-guided-conversational-init' created from master HEAD
start_condition_rule: If ANY start condition is unmet at Phase 1 entry, the Agent fails closed: reports the unmet precondition with diagnostic, writes nothing, and does not begin Phase 1. rc.2 → rc.3 ship order is fixed.

branch_gate.purpose: Machine-readable form of start condition 5, enforced by core/lib/branch-gate.sh on EVERY entry. First entry also requires the current branch tip == local master tip; later entries require the recorded branch_base_sha to remain an ancestor of HEAD (forward advancement only, no re-baseline). The state file .harness/branch-gate.json is recorded once by a successful init and is excluded from the workspace fingerprint + classified mutable in the dirty-worktree manifest (P0-2).

force_stop_rule: F-CONV-09 (Phase 5 acceptance) is the SOLE user phase-stop gate in rc.3. After the final Reviewer PASS on the acceptance package, the Agent presents the complete rc.3 evidence and stops. v2.1+ does NOT auto-start. User must explicitly authorize any further work. Reviewer gates remain INTERNAL progress gates — they gate phase transitions, not user phase-stop.

feature_review_gate.on_pass: feature closes; next feature in Phase 1 proceeds (F-CONV-04→05→06)
feature closes; next feature in Phase 2 proceeds (F-CONV-01→02→03)
feature closes; proceed to Phase 3 cumulative reviewer_gate
feature closes; proceed to Phase 4 cumulative reviewer_gate

phases.title: Acceptance

feature_review_gate.on_pass: feature closes; proceed to Phase 5 cumulative reviewer_gate

phases.user_gate: Explicit user confirmation required before any release action. This is the ONLY user phase-stop gate in rc.3. Reviewer gates are internal progress gates, not user gates.

reviewer_contract.prohibition: Main Agent self-review is prohibited. The Agent that implemented a Phase MUST NOT review its own output.
reviewer_contract.on_unavailable: blocker — Phase cannot proceed; blocker recorded in evidence with missing host capability
reviewer_contract.on_pass: auto-continue to next Phase (user informed, not prompted)
reviewer_contract.on_fail: Agent addresses issues, re-submits for review; retry count recorded

per_feature_gate.applies_to: every feature in every phase — one fresh Reviewer per feature, run BEFORE that phase's cumulative reviewer_gate
per_feature_gate.on_pass: feature closes; next feature in phase proceeds (or phase cumulative review when last feature)
per_feature_gate.verdict_evidence: each feature's verdict is recorded as ORIGINAL evidence (verdict_evidence); the per-phase cumulative reviewer_gate is a SEPARATE review and does NOT overwrite per-feature verdicts

reviewer_contract.scope_note: Two dev-phase review levels: (1) per-feature fresh Reviewer (reviewer_contract.per_feature_gate) then (2) per-phase cumulative Reviewer (reviewer_gate). Both are dev-phase mechanisms only; an independent Reviewer as a permanent runtime gate is a future product concern, deferred until v2.0.0 is stable.

verdict_artifact.purpose: Independent Reviewer verdicts are persisted as append-only evidence. Feature verdicts and phase verdicts are saved SEPARATELY; a phase cumulative review never overwrites per-feature verdict records.

record_schema.purpose: Feature and phase records use SEPARATE schemas (kind split) so a phase cumulative review never shares or overwrites per-feature fields. Validated by core/lib/verdict-artifact.sh (append-only writer + validator).

common.attempt: integer >= 1 — the re-review sequence number; MUST be previous attempt + 1 (validator enforces attempt continuity 1..N with no gaps/duplicates)
common.base_sha: 40- OR 64-hex Git OID — base revision of the reviewed diff (SHA-1 or SHA-256 repos both supported)
common.head_sha: 40- OR 64-hex Git OID — head revision of the reviewed diff; must be a real git object in the project repo
common.run_id: string — associated verification run id. REQUIRED (non-empty) when verdict==PASS; null allowed for FAIL/BLOCKER. When present, must reference an EXISTING, VALID run log (validate_run_log passes)
common.checked: array of strings — spec refs, test-log ids, eval-case ids reviewed

feature_record_extra.feature_id: string — the reviewed feature id (^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_-]*$); must match the artifact file's id

phase_record_extra.feature_ids: array of strings (non-empty) — the phase's feature ids covered by this cumulative review

verdict_artifact.append_rule: each review appends ONE new record with attempt = previous + 1 for the same feature/phase; existing records are never rewritten, truncated, or deleted. A re-review (fix_and_resubmit) writes a NEW record; it does not modify the prior verdict record. The writer computes the next attempt and fully validates the record (schema, attempt continuity, OID format, PASS→non-empty run_id, valid run, real head_sha object) BEFORE appending.

always_independent_authorizations.rule: These operations ALWAYS require explicit in-session user confirmation, regardless of what PROJECT_BRIEF.json says. PROJECT_BRIEF is advisory; session instruction and host security policy take precedence.
operations: external network access (downloads, API calls outside the repo)
destructive_ops (amend, rebase, reset, discard changes, force-push, delete files)

commit_policy.allowed: Ordinary feature commits within the current repository (git add + git commit, conventional messages)
commit_policy.excluded: amend, rebase, reset, discard changes, force-push, and any destructive operations — these ALWAYS require explicit user confirmation

authorization_model: rc.3: advisory Brief + session confirmation. The two-tier loop authorization model (Tier-1 core-enforced + Tier-2 agent-contractual with auth_granted NDJSON) is deferred to a future version after v2.0.0 is stable.

self_host_bootstrap.definition: The harness-companion repo bootstraps ITSELF as a harness project. Bootstrap writes are the ONLY dev-repo writes allowed before Phase 1; they are evidence-of-init, not implementation code.
self_host_bootstrap.state: origin: legacy-unmanaged (manual self-host init, no prior snapshot) → current: managed-valid (valid .template-snapshot.json present). Per frozen §3.4 detection, this bootstrap began with legacy markers (config.json + feature_list/AGENTS/init combo) and no snapshot, and is now managed-valid.
writes: .harness/logs/runs/<run_id>.ndjson (NDJSON init evidence generated via core/harness-verify.sh, NOT hand-crafted)
self_host_bootstrap.verification: Bootstrap is verifiable: config.json passes core/lib/config-validate.sh; snapshot schema_version=1 with real template sources + real SHAs; NDJSON init log generated by harness-verify.sh with run_started + run_completed overall_result=passed; .gitignore contains the three harness entries. Capability level is COMPUTED — 2 (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md knowledge entry + config with verification.commands + feature_list with revision). The knowledge entries and init environment exist NOW as part of the bootstrap; F-CONV-01 does not generate them.
self_host_bootstrap.honesty: generated_by / source_version report the ACTUAL bootstrap baseline (harness-companion v2.0.0-rc.2 @ c5ca212) — never the target v2.0.0-rc.3. Bootstrap origin is legacy-unmanaged (manual, no prior snapshot); current state is managed-valid (valid snapshot). It does not masquerade as rc.3 executor output.
